explanation: Choice C is correct. An expression of the form $x^{2} + bx + c$, where $b$ and $c$ are constants, can be factored if there are two values that add to give $b$ and multiply to give $c$. In the given expression, $b = 5$ and $c = -36$. The values $-4$ and $9$ add to give $5$ and multiply to give $-36$, so the expression can be factored as $\left(x - 4\right)\left(x + 9\right)$. This can be verified by expansion: $\left(x - 4\right)\left(x + 9\right) = x^{2} + 9x - 4x - 36 = x^{2} + 5x - 36$.
